title: SPCX 180-day lock-up cohort's last release — Space Exploration Technologies, 180 days after its 2026-06-11 prospectus
source: SEC: 424B4 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026042639/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm, fetched 2026-10-20 (HTTP 200, 11.95 MB), read in full. Its 'Shares Eligible for Future Sale' table lists "December 8, 2026 (180th day after the date of this prospectus)" as the earliest date the last tranche of the 180-day lock-up cohort is available for sale: "up to 797.6 million shares if the Additional Release Shares were not released on the First Earnings Release Date" (328.4 million if they were). The Additional Release Shares needed SPCX to close >= 30% above the $135 IPO price (>= $175.50) on 5 of the 10 sessions ending 2026-08-04; Yahoo daily closes for 07-20..08-04 peak at $125.33, so the test lapsed and the 797.6 million figure governs. No trigger remains that can move this tranche: the earnings-linked tranches before it are dated by the filing, and the date itself is fixed at 180 days. What it is NOT: the filing's other cohorts (Mr. Musk's shares, 366 days; an extended cohort to the June-2027 quarter's results, together ~7.8 billion shares, >60% of shares outstanding) stay locked and do not release here. One-day wording gap: the filing's lock-up definition ends the period 'immediately after the close of the trading day on the 180th day', while its table says Dec 8 is the earliest date available for sale, so the first full sale session is Dec 8 or Dec 9.
notes: $75.0B offering at $135 (555.6M Class A shares sold; 7,380,196,910 Class A + 5,695,668,265 Class B outstanding after). The 180-day cohort is released in stages (20% after Q2 results on 2026-08-06; 7% on each of 08-20, 09-09, 09-24, 10-09 and 10-24; 28% = ~1.3B shares two full trading days after Q3 results, which SpaceX scheduled for 2026-10-20 after the close, so ~10-22), and this entry is the final stage: up to 797.6M shares, about 17% of the cohort. That is ~10.8% of Class A outstanding and ~1.4x the IPO float, but smaller than the 911.5M (08-06) and 1.3B (~10-22) stages. Read docs/research/events/spcx-lockup-expiry-2026-12-08.md before reading the title as 'the lockup ends'.
